messages:
amelia: quick note — after toggling late-binding for kvcache on staging i saw eviction spike + batch latency regression. dumping details here so we don't lose the thread.

amelia: gist of problem: when we defer attaching reqs to a batch until kernel commit, some KV entries are evicted by the background GC before the kernel reads them. that causes kernel misses and a cascade of small synchronous fetches, which nukes tail latency for a subset of requests.

raj: hmm that rings a bell. are the eviction signals reaching the admission controller? iirc we only emit eviction metrics to observability but not as a control signal.

chris: correct — eviction currently only updates metrics. admission/adaptive-batcher doesn't learn about imminent eviction and so keeps packing requests that will require immediate KV reloads.

amelia: timeline — reproduced on staging at 08:17. stack: continuous-batcher + late-binding + kvcache-gc aggressive policy. i toggled gc to conservative and issue reduced. logs: ```WARN kvcache: entry_evicted key=ctx:abc123 reason=background_gc; span=8ms``` and then kernel shows synchronous `kv_load` for same key.

maria: do we have a quick heuristic: if batcher sees a recent eviction for a prefix, avoid late-binding for that tenant for Xs? or set headroom credits higher?

raj: possible strategies: 1) surface eviction as a soft-pop backpressure signal to admission (increment eviction_score for tenant) 2) during late-binding consider a "probable-miss" estimate using eviction rate & staleness 3) avoid late-binding for tenants with eviction_score > threshold. tradeoff: disables batching optimizations for noisy tenants.

chris: also worth noting: current late-binding window is 120ms. reducing window shrinks exposure but increases number of batches (cost). we need a cost/latency knob.

amelia: tests i ran: reduce window to 40ms -> fewer misses but throughput down 12%. surface eviction -> no throughput hit, latency improved for tails. think 2) + 1) combined might be best.

raj: implementation sketch: add eviction_event stream from kvcache to batcher control plane. eviction_event = {tenant, prefix_hash, ts, reason}. admission keeps sliding window counts per tenant. if eviction_rate > R -> set tenant_mode = "conservative-late-binding".

chris: questions: how to avoid noisy signals from single hot keys? prefix_hash aggregation window or use percentile-based scoring? we should prefer tenant-level signals not key-level.

maria: agree. tenant-level eviction_rate and a "recent_miss_penalty" scalar that decays over time. also we need observability to show when we flip modes.

amelia: also noticed weirdness where eviction spikes correlated with preemption events on nodes (OOM-triggered GC). that suggests routing policy should prefer nodes with cold-started kvcache warmups if possible. preempt-friendly routing might reduce overall misses.

raj: routing layer could prefer nodes with warm cache for that tenant/prefix if we maintain lightweight bloom filters or bloom sketches per node. but that adds state and update traffic. big tradeoff.

chris: alternatives: 1) proactive fetch: when eviction happens, schedule async reload for top N prefixes. 2) increase cache retention for recently-accessed prefixes for Xs after eviction events. 3) cheaper: bump per-tenant headroom credits to allow the kernel to batch the reloads without blocking critical paths.

maria: for short term -> implement eviction_event -> tenant_signal -> flip tenant to conservative late-binding (per-tenant flag) + dashboard panels. Long term -> evaluate bloom-per-node routing or async prefetcher.

amal: typo — my name is amelia ;)

amelia: action items: 
- raj: prototype eviction_event emitter in kvcache (PR targeting staging) — ETA EOD tomorrow
- chris: add admission hook to consume tenant eviction_score and set tenant_mode, and expose metric `tenant.late_binding_mode` — ETA Wed
- maria: dashboard panels and alert if >5% requests hit synchronous kv_loads for >10s — ETA Tue

raj: note on schema: eviction_event should be compact, e.g. `tenant_id, delta_count, window_secs, reason_tags` to keep wire small. maybe sample events for very frequent tenants.

chris: also ensure we don't block the fastpath if admission service is unreachable — fallback to current behavior. add a debug flag to force conservative-late-binding for canary tenants.

maria: unit test ideas: synthetic GC bursts + late-binding on staging, assert tail p95 goes down after flip, and throughput impact measured.

amelia: ok. i'll open a short RFC doc summarizing signal semantics and the minimal control channel. will ping infra-bot to create a staging job id.

infra-bot: created job staging/latebinding-eviction-test-2026-03-20-08 with id sb-7832. logs will be in /var/logs/ci/sb-7832.

raj: thanks — i'll PR the emitter and add a small integration test that posts events to admission.

chris: tagging @maria for dashboards. good thread.

maria: thanks — will sync with observability to avoid metric explosion.

amelia: packing notes: main tradeoffs we chose to mitigate: 1) avoid expensive per-key routing state by using tenant-level signals 2) prefer soft-mode flips (conservative-late-binding) not on/off kills 3) keep a short decay so bursty tenants recover quickly.

amelia: will follow up with RFC link once i draft it.
